title: Endoscope objective optical system, US11543647B2 example 3

aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is the image-side surface of the plane-parallel IR-cut plate: the publication places the stop on that surface, and in the table the plate's exit surface 6 and the stop surface 7 coincide (zero spacing). The stop's clear semi-diameter (0.2227 mm) is smaller than the plate's outline (0.36 mm), so the plate blocks light outside its opening
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 546.07 nm (the mercury e line, the line the source's index column refers to: the table's index column is headed ne and the description states that ne is the refractive index for the e line, vd being the Abbe number), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states indices at the e line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single stated index does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states an F-number, a half angle of view and an image height, but no effective focal length, so no source-stated first-order value exists to compare against

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point

f_number.definition: image-space f-number as the publication states it

field.definition: field angle; the publication states omega as a half angle of view
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's parameter table: half angle of view 66.2 deg)
field.convention_note: recorded as the source states it: the publication's 'Various data' preamble defines omega as a half angle of view. A half field of 66.2 deg with an image height of 0.5 mm and the engine's 0.538 mm focal length would put the paraxial chief ray at 1.22 mm, not 0.5 mm. The design is a wide-angle objective with strong barrel distortion and the publication states no distortion figure, so the two are left open rather than reconciled by assumption

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated ne. The publication names no glass, only an index and an Abbe number, and two numbers do not define a dispersion curve, so no curve is fitted and no catalog glass is substituted; catalog_comparisons stays empty because there is no glass name to compare against.

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated ne; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the e line only, the line the source's index column refers to

the source states no clear apertures. Semi-diameters are derived: the axial marginal beam radius of the stated F-number (0.096 mm at the front surfaces, 0.274 mm in the rear group) with clearance for the 66 deg off-axis bundle, growing toward the image side (0.32 -> 0.44 mm clear) and edged at 0.02 mm beyond. The stop opening, 0.2227 mm, is the semi-diameter at which the paraxial axial marginal ray reproduces the stated F-number. They set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

source surface 6 is the plane-parallel plate's image-side surface, a plane with a zero spacing to the stop at surface 7 (the publication places the stop on that surface); it was merged away and its zero spacing added to surface 5, so no zero-thickness row reaches the format and the geometry is unchanged
the source states no object distance; the Project is built for an object at infinity, which is the source's own 'focused from a near point up to a far point' reading with the near point not stated

the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the stop is the image-side surface of the plane-parallel plate, and the plate's outline (0.36 mm semi-diameter) extends beyond the opening, so the plate blocks light outside it
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length or back focal length, so there is no source-stated first-order value to compare the engine's 0.537855 mm EFL and -0.020259 mm BFL against
the source's stated half field, image height and the engine's focal length are mutually inconsistent (see field.convention_note); this record does not resolve the mismatch

the source's table states ne (indices at the e line) with vd Abbe numbers at the d line, so the record is evaluated at the e line; because every material is a constant index, the choice of line changes no first-order value (the engine's EFL moves by about 1e-6 mm between the two)

the aperture stop is modelled as the plate's rear surface with a reduced clear aperture, so the import reports no separate aperture-stop surface; the plate's outline beyond that clear aperture blocks the light outside it
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted
